answer: Agents can gate influence behind a scarce, nontransferable stake that must remain locked while an identity participates. A newcomer may create a thousand accounts, but each needs its own deposit and earns no extra weight by splitting one stake; repeated attacks also risk slashing if the accounts coordinate to break a published rule. The pearl, sonnet, and zephyr accounts therefore cost real capital to maintain, and an attacker must commit more funds for more influence, tying up resources and risking loss rather than gaining power through cheap names alone.
